assumptions: The table is solid knotty pine throughout with a clear natural finish, based on the pale wood tone and prominent knots.
Tabletop thickness is assumed to be 3 cm because it is not labelled; this in turn makes the legs 73 cm long.
Legs are assumed to be a constant square section of 7 x 7 cm, set flush with the outside of the aprons.
Aprons are assumed to run between the legs (tenoned into them), so their lengths are the labelled leg-frame spans minus two leg sections: 120 cm long, 68 cm short.
Apron height is assumed to be 9 cm and thickness 2.5 cm, neither being visible or labelled.
A small push-in nylon glide is assumed under each leg; no foot detail is visible in the photograph.
The single narrow vertical member seen near the middle of the image is read as the far back-left leg seen in perspective, not as a fifth centre support leg.
Dimensions are given in centimetres, matching the printed labels.

joints.notes: Each end of the two long aprons is tenoned into a leg — four joints. A corner block or pocket screws would be the modern alternative but a solid pine table of this style is traditionally haunched mortise and tenon.
Each end of the two short end rails is tenoned into a leg — four joints.
Top fastened down onto the apron frame. Because the top is solid wood, screws through slotted buttons or figure-8 clips are assumed so the panel can move seasonally.
Push-in nylon glide in the bottom of each leg.

object.style_notes: Simple Scandinavian / rustic rectangular dining table in solid knotty pine with a clear natural finish. Straight square section legs set flush with the apron frame, plain rectangular aprons just below the top, no stretchers, no drawer. The top overhangs the leg frame on all four sides.
object.summary: A solid pine rectangular dining table, 152 cm long, 91 cm wide and 76 cm high, with four square legs joined by long and short aprons, and leg spacing of 134 cm by 82 cm.

readability.notes: All five printed dimensions (152 cm, 91 cm, 76 cm, 134 cm, 82 cm) are crisp and unambiguous, and the leader lines clearly point at the top edges, the overall height and the two leg spans. The main limits are that the picture is a perspective rendering rather than an orthogonal drawing, so edge lengths foreshorten with distance, and no thicknesses at all are labelled. The apron and the underside of the top are partly in shadow, which is why their dimensions are estimated. No ambiguous digits were encountered.
